content.text: Vitamin
Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid):
Greek 'pantos' = everywhere
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine /Pyridoxal /Pyridoxamine)
Vitamin B7 (Biotin)
RDA (Adults)
Blood pantothenic acid: 1.57–2.79 µmol/L
AI: 5 mg/day (adults)                             No UL
Plasma PLP(pyridoxal-5-phosphate): +30 nmol/L
RDA: 1.3–1.7 mg/day                                        UL: 100 mg/day
Serum biotin: 133–329 pmol/L
AI: 30 µg/day                                          No UL
Food Sources
almost all foods; avocado, sweet potato, whole grains
Meat, liver, kidney, Sunflower seeds, mushrooms
Meat, poultry, fish
Potatoes, starchy veggies, chickpeas, legumes, bananas, fortified cereals
Egg yolks, liver, kidney, nuts, seeds (almond, sunflower), sweet potato, legumes
Gut bacteria synthesize some biotin
Absorption & Storage
- Absorbed throughout sm intestine, min storage
-Converted to Coenzyme A (CoA): essential cofactor in Krebs, fatty
acid synth/oxidation, cholesterol synth & +100 metabolic rxn
- Absorbed in jejunum, stored as PLP bound to muscle phosphorylase
- Active form: pyridoxal-5-phosphate (PLP): coenzyme for +100 enzymatic rxn
- AA metabolism, NT synth (5-HT, DA, GABA, norepi), hgb synth, glycogenolysis
- Absorbed in sm intestine, bound to enzymes as biotinyl-lysine
5 carboxylase enzymes cofactor: pyruvate carboxylase, acetyl-CoA carboxylase
(fatty acid synth), propionyl-CoA carboxylase, methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase
- Raw egg whites contain avidin: binds biotin & prevent absorb
Deficiency Effects & Causes
DEFICIENCY (extremely rare):
- Burning feet syndrome (paresthesia, pain, numbness in feet)
- Fatigue, HA, irritability, GI disturbances
- only in severe global malnutrition or w specific antagonist
(omega-methylpantothenate)
Causes: almost no isolated deficiency in clin practice
DEFICIENCY:      Sz (neonates w B6-dep epilepsy)
- Periph neuropathy (symmetrical), ↑homocysteine (♡vasc risk)
- Seborrheic dermatitis, glossitis, angular cheilitis, confusion, irritability, depression
- Microcytic, hypochromic anemia (impaired heme synth)
Causes: poor diet, alcoholism, malabsorb, INH/isoniazid tx (gives B6 antagonist effect), penicillamine, oral contraceptives (↑B6 metabolism), elderly
DEFICIENCY (rare):
- Alopecia (hair thinning/loss), conjunctivitis, brittle nails
- Scaly, seborrheic dermatitis (perioral, periorbital)
- Neurologic: depression, lethargy, paresthesias, ataxia
Causes: prolonged eat raw egg white (avidin), ↓biotinidase (genetic), long-term anticonvulsant, parenteral nutrition w.o biotin, prolonged abx use
Toxicity (Excess) Effects & Causes
TOXICITY:
Very low toxicity
High doses (>10 g/day): GI distress, diarrhea
No established UL
TOXICITY (from supp - NOT from food):         - Photosensitivity, skin lesions
- Sensory neuropathy, ataxia (numbness, burning pain, loss of proprioception)
MC irreversible if prolonged
Causes: doses >200 mg/day chronically; neurotoxicity well-documented
TOXICITY: No known toxicity — no UL established
- HIGH doses interfere w immunoassay-based lab tests (troponin, TSH, PTH,
hCG) -> false ↓or↑ — clin sig
Causes: widely consumed in high-dose 'hair/nail/skin' supp
Supp Commonly Needed?
No: normal diet in virtually all pop
Yes: isoniazid-tx pt (routine co-Rx), alcoholics, elderly, preg-related nausea (B6 + doxylamine = Diclegis/Bonjesta), AFAB BC PO w depression
Rare; yes: ↓biotinidase (neonatal screening), prolonged TPN, anticonvulsant tx
CAUTION: high-dose biotin supp interfere w lab tests
Uses
